<description>
Enable some bugprone clang-tidy checks, which seem useful.

Apart from a test-only bug, they didn't find anything severe, but I think it still makes sense to enable them, so that it is easier to read the resulting code. Also, it is trivial to disable them, if they turn out annoying.
</description>

<commits>
fab3062590 refactor: Enable bugprone-unused-raii

The code change does not change any behavior, because the name is not
used in the compile-time context.

fa8c949e4c refactor: Enable bugprone-string-literal-with-embedded-nul

Also, fix a test bug.

fa077e9f79 refactor: Enable bugprone-inaccurate-erase

Also, instead of using the erase-remove idiom consistenly, just use the
C++20 std::erase here.

Note: Wallets are unique, so the code change does not change any
behavior.

fa3384c36a refactor: Enable some useful bugprone checks, which are clean right now

Also, sort

fa60b2ae8d refactor: Enable bugprone-return-const-ref-from-parameter to find missing LIFETIMEBOUND annotations

Whenever the check fires, a missing LIFETIMEBOUND should be added.
</commits>
